For Entailment/Contradiction, identify the exact evidence segment IDs.

Use human feedback to improve the correctness of your labels and evidence IDs.

Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-11 (No reverse engineering): No mention of reverse engineering anywhere. NotMentioned.

nda-16 (Return of confidential information): No mention of returning or destroying information upon termination. NotMentioned.

nda-15 (No licensing): No explicit statement that agreement grants no rights to Confidential Information. NotMentioned.

nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): No mention of not disclosing the existence of the agreement. NotMentioned.

nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical information): Segment [3] lists "security set-up, security architecture, lay-out, security processes and procedures, designs, drawings, software and hardware configuration, computer programs, algorithms, services, customers etc" — this includes non-technical items like "services, customers". So the hypothesis that CI shall ONLY include technical information is Contradicted by [3].

nda-1 (Explicit identification): Segment [7] says "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing". Since it can be provided verbally or not reduced in writing, it's not all expressly identified. Contradiction with evidence [7].

nda-19 (Survival of obligations): Segment [29] says term continues until Discloser terminates or premises relocated/vacated/abandoned. No mention of obligations surviving termination. NotMentioned.

nda-12 (Permissible development of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): Segment [7] mentions information "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing". Entailment with evidence [7].

nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment [10] says Recipient agrees not to share with any Third Party. This contradicts the hypothesis that Recipient MAY share with third parties. Contradiction with evidence [10].

nda-17 (Permissible copy): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [11] says Recipient must prevent disclosure "even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser". This requires express permission (which implies some form of seeking permission), but does it require notification? It says "without the express permission of the Discloser" — this is stronger than notice; it requires permission. The hypothesis says "shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose". Requiring express permission arguably entails notification/communication with the Discloser. Hmm. This is a judgment call. The clause requires express permission before disclosure under law, which implies the Recipient must approach the Discloser (a form of notice). I'd lean Entailment with evidence [11]. But strictly, "notify" vs "obtain permission" — obtaining permission necessarily requires informing. I'll consider Entailment.

nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Segment [10] says not to share with any Third Party. Employees of the Recipient are typically not third parties. The agreement doesn't explicitly permit sharing with employees. Hmm. The Purpose requires installation of CCTV, implying employees would need access. But strictly, the document doesn't mention employees. NotMentioned seems safer. Actually, in many NDA audit datasets, "sharing with employees" is often NotMentioned when no employee clause exists. NotMentioned.

nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [10] "No Use: Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" — but the Purpose is stated in [5] (supply, installation, testing and commissioning of CCTV). Recipient gets access for the Purpose. The hypothesis: "shall not use CI for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Segment [10] says no use in any way, but [5] and [7] imply access for the Purpose. Segment [15] says access to layout plan for the purpose of carrying out the contract. This supports limited use for the Purpose. Evidence: [10] (no use) combined with [5]/[15] (purpose). Entailment with evidence [10] and possibly [5]. I'd say Entailment with [10] primarily.

Thought: The feedback says "Contain Irrelevant Evidences" for nda-8 with evidence [11]. This suggests either segment [11] is not the right evidence, or the label should be NotMentioned, or additional/different segments are needed.

Segment [11]: "2.2 No Unauthorized Disclosure: Recipient agrees to use its best efforts to prevent and protect the Confidential Information, or any part thereof, from disclosure to any person(s) or entity(ies), even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser."

This says the Recipient must prevent disclosure even if directed under law, without express permission. The hypothesis nda-8 is about notifying the Discloser when required by law to disclose. The clause requires "express permission" — which implies communication, but the feedback says [11] is irrelevant evidence. Perhaps the intended label is NotMentioned, since the clause doesn't mention notification — it actually prohibits disclosure under law entirely unless permission granted. The hypothesis about "notice on compelled disclosure" typically requires a notification obligation, which this clause doesn't explicitly state — it requires permission, not notice. So the label might be NotMentioned.
